items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the way I got into George Hudson’s band in St. Louis... That opened the door for me for George Hudson’s band.

ctx.x: Yeah. I wanted to listen to your thoughts. I have my [ ? ? ].

I loved what Beiderbecke played. Same as Hackett. I love Hackett. Hackett was – I knew very well, a very dear friend of mine, a beautiful player. As a matter of fact, the way I got into George Hudson’s band in St. Louis was that Glenn Miller had a hit record called [Terry sings]. What’s the name of that? [A String of Pearls]. And Hackett
had a solo on it [Terry sings the solo]. What’s the name of that? [Terry sings the theme again.] Remember that?

items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: Oh, with George Hudson’s band? ... Yeah. ... With Hudson’s band, wasn’t it? ... Yeah.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. I was thinking about, long before then I came through there with, let’s see in ‘43 I came through the first time, with Lionel Hampton. And then you, they was telling us about this trumpet player who played lead and also was the best soloist they had, which, you were doing it all about that time.
